summary: Backend testing of Bill-side Multi-Pay (POST /api/companies/{cid}/transactions/{tid}/receive-payment). All 5 existing pytest tests in test_multi_bill_pay.py pass (5/5). Additional live-URL API smoke test confirms: 200 multi-bill settlement (2 bills → 1 payment), correct 400 rejects for mixed apps / cap violation / bill-on-deposit, txn stamped with A/P + linked_payment_id + posted=true, and list enrichment exposes linked_applications_count=2 / linked_applications_total=300. HOWEVER, a CRITICAL data-integrity bug was discovered: the bills read endpoints (bills/{bid} and bills list) recompute balance_due only from payments with matching linked_bill_id, ignoring the new `applications` array — so for multi-bill payments every SECONDARY bill (all bills except the largest 'primary') has its persisted balance_due silently reset back to `total` on the very next GET, even though `status` is correctly 'paid'. The invoices side already handles both sources (Mar 2026 fix at /app/backend/routes/invoices.py line ~395-410 unions singular linked_invoice_id AND $unwind applications) — the bill parity update was missed. Frontend UI could not be exercised e2e because the test client user (client@axiom.ai) is currently attached only to an un-onboarded 'AutoSwitchCo 1786792423' company (Skyward Sparks LLC listed in memory/test_credentials.md does not exist for this login), and the frontend Transactions route is gated behind onboarding. Frontend code review of LinkModal (line ~4258) and LinkedDocChip (line ~56) shows correct implementation for both invoice+bill kinds; data-testids present.

critical.issue: Self-heal reconciliation of balance_due sums payments only by linked_bill_id, ignoring the multi-app `applications` array. Secondary bills in any multi-bill payment get balance_due reset from 0 back to their original total on next read (verified with a $100 + $200 bill paid by one -$300 txn: bill1 status=paid but balance_due stayed 100.0 after multi-pay + subsequent GET). Impacts A/P aging, bill amount_paid display, and any downstream consumer of persisted balance_due. Invoices already handle this correctly at /app/backend/routes/invoices.py ~L395-460 — mirror that union in bills.py list_bills (L88-111) and get_bill (L115-137).

minor.issue: 500 KeyError: 'code' at routes/transactions.py:1425 when auto_categorize=True (default) and no category_account_id supplied, if any account doc in that company lacks a `code` field. Preexisting, not in scope for this review, but blocks a common code path. Fix: `a.get('code','')` in the coa list comprehension.

critical_code_review_comments: receive_payment_multi (transactions.py ~L2208-2421) is well-structured with symmetric invoice/bill handling, cap enforcement, direction guard, and reverse-of-prior-payment. Good.

The 'primary' bill selection is `max(enriched_apps, key=lambda a: a['amount'])` which is deterministic but can produce a different single linked_bill_id on ties; downstream displays already use the applications array via linked_applications_count, so this is fine — but the missed side effect is that the read-side balance_due self-heal uses linked_bill_id exclusively, hence the reported HIGH bug.

rca of the issue: Multi-bill payment write path correctly persists balance_due=0 on each applied bill via db.bills.update_one at routes/transactions.py:2385-2389. However, on the very next read the bills.py self-heal recomputes balance_due as `total - sum(payments where linked_bill_id == this_bill_id)`. Because the payment doc stores only ONE `linked_bill_id` (the 'primary'/largest app), the aggregate returns 0 for every non-primary bill, so expected_bal = total - 0 = total, and the code overwrites the persisted 0 with `total`. Invoices side (invoices.py L389-410) was retrofitted in Mar 2026 to also union payments matched by `applications.invoice_id` via $unwind; bills.py was not updated in parity. Reproduction: create bills B1=$100, B2=$200; withdrawal txn T=-$300; POST /receive-payment with both apps. Payment inserted with linked_bill_id=B2 (primary) + applications=[{B1,100},{B2,200}]. GET /bills/B1 → recomputes 0 payments matched → resets balance_due to 100 while status stays 'paid'. Mitigation: patch bills.py aggregate + get_bill payment sum to include applications-array matches, mirroring invoices.py.
